title: An Australian platform worker resumed work after voluntary reactivation and later received a formal access-restoration order
source_unit: One Australian platform worker and Fair Work Commission proceeding; adjudicated same-case remedy follow-up, not a population estimate

observations.period: 2025-04-08 to 2025-09-23; deactivation, reactivation, post-reactivation work, and formal order

access_restoration.value: Uber voluntarily reactivated access on 2025-05-19; the Full Bench later ordered reactivation

continued_work.value: more than 150 trips completed after reactivation by 2025-07-21

financial_remedy.value: lost-remuneration quantum remained open and was directed for party consultation
financial_remedy.unit: formal remedy stage; payment not observed

observations.method: Read the primary Fair Work Commission Full Bench and merits records as a dated single-case sequence, preserving voluntary reactivation, subsequent trip activity, formal order, and the separate open lost-pay stage.
observations.uncertainty: The public record does not establish net earnings, expenses, payment receipt, account status after the trip count, profile or rating correction, alternative work, recurrence protection, anti-retaliation, household recovery, trust change, collective action, or exit. One Australian case cannot estimate platform incidence or typical remedy effectiveness.
observations.subgroup: Single case: Mohammad Shareef Hotak and Uber Driver Platform / Rasier Pacific
observations.counterinterpretation: More than 150 trips show operational return to work, not unconstrained choice, financial recovery, or durable protection. Continued platform use may reflect dependence or lack of alternatives; the later formal order shows voluntary reactivation did not settle the legal or financial remedy question.

related_sources.claim: The Full Bench merits record preserves the formal reactivation order and open lost-remuneration stage.
The committed local memo records the dates, 150-plus trips, remedy stages, and boundary.

boundary: This comparative Australian case closes voluntary access restoration and subsequent observed work activity before a formal access-restoration order. It does not close payment, net recovery, alternative work, durable protection, trust, collective action, or practical exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Existing committed local Hotak follow-up memo and targeted official decision URLs; no bulk archive retained
